clay.summary: MOSAIC is retained and specialized: add authoritative event-spine + durable derivation/outbox semantics and Cognitive State Continuity Loop as a concrete persistence mechanism; keep physical monolith benchmark-gated.

frank.summary: C6 one-semantic-world target should lower onto UD-RC1: exact state/effect commit spine, unified ClayCode query IR, derived graph/vector/FTS/activation, isolated capability secrets, background cognitive-state continuity.

claycode.summary: Add UnifiedQueryIR and receipts for physical route choices, derivation lag/rebuild recipe and authorized selection space; planner optimization may not weaken operation-specific semantic closure.

claygraph.summary: Treat ClayGraph as a specialized semantic/associative projection in the unified fabric; graph activation consumes canonical event deltas and may evolve between model calls, but remains non-authoritative and epoch-bound. Compare automatic activation against explicit retrieval/no-memory controls.

hyperposition.summary: H4 semantic firebreaks remain necessary. UnifiedDB adds physical-placement and derived-lag witnesses to operation-specific basis; one semantic substrate must remain compartmentalized across authority and derived planes.

gwt.summary: Database/activation/retrieval effects must remain orthogonal to workspace selection. Future GWT lesions must pin query-plan, derived-view, activation epoch and candidate-set identities when attributing workspace effects.

emergenz.summary: Use UnifiedDB receipts to identify intervention episodes and persistent-state continuity, but do not treat integration or autonomous activation as evidence of emergence or consciousness.

unifieddb.summary: Foundation narrows to UD-RC1 default: semantic/logical unification + authoritative event/state spine + replayable derived sidecars + Cognitive State Continuity Loop; physical consolidation remains workload-specific.

ancestry_warning: Clay G11 and UnifiedDB U1 are same-RAE sequential evidence; agreement is refinement/convergence, not independent replication.
